reviewer_type: AI-assisted claim-level source audit with independent read-only post-edit reviews; no human expert review is claimed.
title: Pereboom’s Four-Case Argument
scope: Claim-level traceability review of the complete article, matching dataset record, and expansion entry. Focus: the four-case progression and like-cases inference; the specified cases and compatibilist-friendly capacities; under-description and disagreement; hard- and soft-line replies; the target of basic-desert responsibility; related manipulation arguments; publication metadata; and accurate disclosure of primary-text access. This status follows the approved standard’s allowance for another appropriate source when relevant passages are read; it does not claim direct verification against Pereboom’s 2001 Chapter 4 or expert review.
summary: Full relevant passages in the archived SEP supplement, current SEP entry, Jeppsson’s peer-reviewed analysis, and Caruso’s précis support the article’s narrowed paraphrase of the cases, conditional inference, known disagreement, and basic-desert scope. The article no longer implies that the primary 2001 chapter was read: Google Books lists Chapter 4 but exposes selected image-only pages rather than its argument text; an online excerpt’s provenance remains unverified and is not treated as verified book text. A targeted independent post-edit reviewer passed the revised access disclosure. An earlier reviewer preferred a partial status because the primary chapter was inaccessible; this ledger adopts source_checked for the declared paraphrase/traceability scope because the appropriate full secondary passages were read and the access limit is explicit. No expert review is claimed.

claim_evidence.material_claim: Pereboom’s four cases move from direct moment-to-moment manipulation, to birth programming, to upbringing, and then to an ordinary agent in a deterministic world; the inference appeals to treating relevantly like cases alike.
claim_evidence.exact_location: Introduction, “The argument,” including the sequence from electronic intervention to programming/upbringing and Case 4; corroborated by Jeppsson §1, pp. 1935–1937.
claim_evidence.finding: The article describes the sequence and makes the inference conditional: a responsibility-relevant difference that blocks the transition to Case 4 would undermine the argument.
claim_evidence.limitation: The cases’ comparability and the like-cases principle are contested; no claim is made that the argument is proven sound.
claim_evidence.required_edit: Made: presented the transition as an argument with a conditional premise, not as an established equivalence.

claim_evidence.material_claim: Case 1 uses radio-like technology to manipulate Plum’s decisions and actions moment by moment while stipulating compatibilist-friendly capacities, including reasons-responsive deliberation.
claim_evidence.source_title: The Agential Perspective: A Hard-Line Reply to the Four-Case Manipulation Argument
claim_evidence.exact_location: Jeppsson §1, pp. 1935–1936; archived SEP supplement, “The argument,” describing direct electronic stimulation and moment-to-moment decisions/actions.
claim_evidence.finding: The article now says that technology manipulates decisions and actions moment by moment, rather than implying a distinct alteration of reasoning ability; it separately states that reasons-responsive deliberation is stipulated.
claim_evidence.limitation: The article is a stylized thought experiment and compresses case details; no verbatim quotation from the inaccessible 2001 chapter is presented.
claim_evidence.required_edit: Made: changed “manipulate Plum’s reasoning” to “manipulate Plum’s decisions and actions” and kept reasons-responsiveness as a separate stipulation.

claim_evidence.material_claim: The move from the first three cases to ordinary determinism is disputed because the first three cases are under-described and different completions may change whether a responsibility-relevant difference exists.
claim_evidence.exact_location: §3.2, “Manipulation and Design Arguments,” passages on the first three Plum cases’ under-description, the relevance of how details are filled in, and objections to the inference.
claim_evidence.finding: The article accurately reports that case details and reader verdicts are contested and does not state that the transition is universally accepted.
claim_evidence.limitation: The brief article does not catalog every response or each proposed detail that could matter.
claim_evidence.required_edit: Made: added the current SEP qualification that the first three cases are under-described and verdicts can vary with specification.

claim_evidence.material_claim: Hard-line replies deny that manipulation undermines responsibility or press for the same verdict in ordinary deterministic cases; soft-line replies accept the manipulation verdict but claim an ethically relevant difference from ordinary histories.
claim_evidence.source_title: The Agential Perspective: A Hard-Line Reply to the Four-Case Manipulation Argument
claim_evidence.exact_location: Jeppsson §1, pp. 1936–1937, where the hard-line and soft-line reply labels and strategies are explained; archived SEP supplement, “The distinction,” for the premise-level strategy distinction.
claim_evidence.finding: The article describes both strategies as competing replies and explicitly says neither is settled.
claim_evidence.limitation: The categories simplify a literature with multiple variants and do not imply that every author uses the labels identically.
claim_evidence.required_edit: Made: attributed the taxonomy to Jeppsson and framed the responses as competing positions.

claim_evidence.material_claim: The target is basic-desert responsibility; rejecting that kind of desert does not by itself decide whether protective, rehabilitative, or other forward-looking responses are justified.
claim_evidence.source_title: Précis of Derk Pereboom’s Free Will, Agency, and Meaning in Life
claim_evidence.exact_location: Opening paragraphs defining basic-desert praise/blame and the discussion summarizing Chapter 6’s forward-looking account of moral responsibility.
claim_evidence.finding: The article distinguishes basic-desert blame/praise from other possible responses and avoids claiming that skepticism entails abandoning all practical responses to wrongdoing.
claim_evidence.limitation: Caruso summarizes Pereboom’s 2014 book; this is secondary context, not primary evidence for the 2001 chapter wording.
claim_evidence.required_edit: Made: stated the basic-desert target and kept practical responses open.

claim_evidence.material_claim: Mele’s Ernie/Bert case is related to, but not simply another name for, Pereboom’s four-case argument.
claim_evidence.exact_location: §3.2, “Manipulation and Design Arguments,” on Mele’s zygote argument and its structure relative to other manipulation arguments.
claim_evidence.finding: The article identifies a family resemblance but notes that causal histories and replies differ.
claim_evidence.limitation: The entry gives only a brief comparison; the article does not claim to compare every manipulation argument.
claim_evidence.required_edit: Made: labelled Mele’s argument as a related but distinct comparison.

claim_evidence.exact_location: Book record and contents list Chapter 4, “Problems for Compatibilism,” beginning at p. 89; selected image-only preview pages include title/contents and bibliography/index, not readable Chapter 4 text.
claim_evidence.finding: The article and data now say Chapter 4 is listed but its text is not exposed; an unsupported Internet Archive access statement was removed.

claim_evidence.required_edit: Made: corrected “title-page preview only” to describe selected pages accurately and removed the unverified Internet Archive claim.

edits_made: Narrowed the case descriptions and made the inference to Case 4 explicitly conditional on the absence of a responsibility-relevant difference.
Changed Case 1 wording to match sources’ moment-to-moment manipulation of decisions and actions, while preserving the separate reasons-responsive stipulation.
Added current SEP support for under-description, disagreement, and related Mele comparison; bounded hard-/soft-line claims to cited analyses.
Clarified basic-desert scope and that protective or rehabilitative responses are not thereby ruled out.
Corrected the Google Books selected-page disclosure in article and data; removed the unsupported Internet Archive access assertion; retained the excerpt-provenance caveat.

A publicly hosted excerpt was consulted, but its publication container and identity with the 2001 edition remain unverified; it is excluded as evidence for the material claims.
Whether the cases are sufficiently specified and whether manipulation undermines responsibility remain disputed; no philosophical verdict is claimed.

The Google Books support text now correctly describes selected pages and the unavailable Chapter 4 text. No public source-review status field was added.
further_reading_matches: All five article Further Reading URLs match the dataset record in the same order.
risk_reason: The article explains a contested philosophical argument whose primary book chapter was not directly accessible; exact case details, attribution, and access disclosure therefore require careful separation of primary metadata from full secondary analyses.
audit_focus: Check the four-case sequence and replies against appropriate full scholarly sources; preserve disagreement and under-description; verify the basic-desert scope; correct the Google Books preview disclosure; record the primary-text and excerpt provenance limits.
independent_review: One independent reviewer supported the narrowed case content but conservatively preferred partially_source_checked because the 2001 chapter text was not accessible and the preview description was imprecise. After correction, a targeted independent reviewer passed the Google Books disclosure and recommended source_checked under the standard’s allowance for another appropriate source, while keeping the primary-text caveat explicit. The ledger adopts source_checked for the declared claim-traceability scope because relevant full passages in SEP and Jeppsson support the paraphrases; direct primary-text verification and excerpt provenance remain disclosed limits. No expert review.
